definitions.explanation: A rigid, box-shaped leather or synthetic backpack used by Japanese elementary school children. Traditionally red for girls and black for boys, though many colors are now available.

examples.japanese: ランドセル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{背負|せお}って→背負う：16159_seou⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: Go to school carrying a randoseru on your back.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦{入学|にゅうがく}する→入学する：01851_nyuugakusuru⟧⟦{孫|まご}→孫：03731_mago⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ランドセル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。
examples.english: I bought a school backpack for my grandchild who starts school next year.

examples.english: Modern school backpacks are colorful — not just red and black but also purple and light blue are popular.

notes:
ランドセル comes from the Dutch word "ransel" (backpack), introduced during the Meiji period when the Japanese military adopted Western-style equipment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ランドセル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{背負|せお}う→背負う：16159_seou⟧ (carry a randoseru on one's back)
- ランドセル⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧ (buy a randoseru)
- ランドセル⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (put in a randoseru)
- ⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧ランドセル (red randoseru)

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Used exclusively by elementary school students (grades 1-6)
- Purchasing a ランドセル is a major event for families, often done by grandparents as a gift
- High-quality models can cost ¥50,000-¥100,000 or more
- ラン{活|かつ} ("ran-katsu") refers to the competitive process of choosing and buying one, often starting over a year before enrollment
- The rigid design protects textbooks and provides back support for young children
